Method of Attack: SQL injection (SQLi) vulnerability leading to escalated privileges and unauthorized access
Critical SQL injection vulnerabilities allowing unauthenticated attackers to compromise unpatched and Internet-exposed servers to steal customer information
Zero-day exploit used by Clop ransomware gang for data theft
Discoverer: Huntress Senior Security Researcher John Hammond
Impacted Systems: Organizations including Shell, University of Georgia (UGA), University System of Georgia (USG), UnitedHealthcare Student Resources (UHSR), Heidelberger Druck, Landal Greenparks, Zellis (and customers BBC, Boots, Aer Lingus, Ireland's HSE), Ofcam, government of Nova Scotia, US states of Missouri and Illinois, University of Rochester, American Board of Internal Medicine, BORN Ontario, Extreme Networks, several U.S. federal agencies, U.S. Department of Energy entities
Attack Vector: Exploitation of SQL injection vulnerabilities in MOVEit Transfer web application
Compromise through HTTP and HTTPS traffic before patching
Indicators of Compromise: Dark web data leak site listing extorted organizations
Proof-of-concept exploit code shared on Twitter
